question.worked_solution:
Let's remind ourselves of the special trigonometric ratios, as given by the unit circle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250054/assets/dbf36192ac332dc49ed75278838e989a37ac7d888311be1b8b059a7b59667aa6.png)

From the unit circle, we see that the angle $\frac{7\pi }{6}$ corresponds to the point $(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},-\frac{1}{2}).$

Since the cosine of the angle corresponds to the $x$-coordinate, we have $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$

Therefore, using the fact that $\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})}=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}=-\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}.
$$
